To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) depth-based face verification can be efficiently performed by leveraging the privileged information of the RGB modality, (b) the proposed JanusNet is able to extract complementary features from depth and RGB images, (c) depth-based face recognition can be efficiently performed in real time, and (d) depth-based face identification can be performed with state-of-art performance on a variety of head poses, occlusions, and illumination changes.
we propose a deep architecture for face verification from depth, that achieves state-of-the-art results and real-time performance, despite the limited amount of data available for training.

In summary, our research is concerned with

the problem of face verification from a depth map, and it is motivated by two key observations: i) depth data are not widely used for face recognition, despite their robustness against illumination variations, and ii) there is a lack of depth-based datasets, which are essential to the development of new algorithms for face verification.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed approach is able to efficiently verify if two face images, captured from different viewpoints and under different illuminations, belong to the same identity.

the proposed approach achieves state-of-art performance on the challenging 300-VW and BU-3DFE depth-based face verification benchmarks, while outperforming the current state-of-art RGB-based models on the 300-VW benchmark, and being competitive on the Labeled Face in the Wild benchmark.
the proposed method outperforms state-of-art methods on two public benchmarks, and achieves real time performance, while relying on depth images only.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are the first to show that depth data is a good alternative to RGB data for face verification and that we can use a hybrid network to learn complementary features.
we propose a novel deep architecture for depth-based verification that achieves state of the art results and real time inference.
, given the current lack of depth oriented datasets for face verification, we have developed a novel approach that can be applied to depth data without requiring a large training set.
The main takeaway from our work is that
depth images are a promising modality for face recognition and that the combination of RGB and depth data can be beneficial for face verification.
depth information can be successfully used to improve face recognition performance, especially when the available data is limited and the training process is constrained.
